nodes.title: Exact n=2 symmetric INF M3 system
nodes.statement: For R > 1 and u = R^(-1/6), the M3 problem is the exact real four-equation system E1 = E2 = E5 = E6 = 0 bound in the frozen problem contract, with k2 = K(u)u, k3 = K(u)u + Cbr(u)u^5, p1 = pi/2 + A(u)u^2, and p3 = pi/4 + B(u)u^2. Every admitted asymptotic assertion must correspond to the exact finite-R real symmetric band-consistent n=2 INF branch and is restricted to M3.

nodes.title: Corrected M3 observable and determinant normalization
nodes.statement: On the finite-interior n=2 symmetric INF germ, Cbr denotes the positive branch coefficient in k3 = K(u)u + Cbr(u)u^5 and is distinct from Chi_up = 1 + B(u)K(u)/2 + 3pi/(2K(u)) - K(u)^2/12. The quantities m3D and m3N are the exact D-side and N-side third-block masses from the closed residual. Kp_odd and Ko are the full two-by-two sector matrices in the exact orthonormal mirror bases, with the source spectral pole convention and reduced-Green finite part Gt = L0 + Lminus/2 fixed by the bound normalization package.

nodes.title: Exact even analytic finite-R INF branch
nodes.statement: Let kappa = (18pi - 48/pi)^(1/3). There exist u0 > 0 and M < infinity and an exact locally unique real-analytic even branch in the finite nonzero interior chart for every 0 < u < u0 on which E1 = E2 = E5 = E6 = 0, K(u) = kappa + O(u^2), A(u) = 2/kappa + O(u^2), B(u) = 1/kappa + O(u^2), Cbr(u) = 16/(pi kappa) + O(u^2), K1 = C1 = 0, and k3 - k2 = (16/(pi kappa))u^5 + O(u^7), with the corresponding absolute remainder bounds. For every R > u0^(-6), this root is a nondegenerate real symmetric band-consistent n=2 INF branch with positive widths and the lambda_2 and lambda_3 indexing certified in the proof package.

nodes.title: Exact blow-up and finite-R branch proof
nodes.statement: The exact M3 problem hypothesis implies the locally unique even analytic finite-R branch theorem after two exact blow-ups, a nonzero seed Jacobian certificate, analytic implicit continuation, and the finite-R branch-selection and nodal-sign audit.

nodes.title: Admitted-class scale exhaustiveness
nodes.statement: Within the finite nonzero interior limiting class where K stays in a compact subset of (0,infinity), p1 tends to pi/2, p3 tends to pi/4, k3/k2 tends to 1, and the listed phase denominators stay separated from zero, every exact zero branch is the unique analytic germ in v = u^2 from CLM-R001-FINITE-R-BRANCH-V1. Thus no distinct rational-Puiseux, logarithmic, inverse-logarithmic, mixed power-log, odd-power, flat, or non-transseries exact correction branch exists in this admitted class. The singular geometries K tending to 0 or infinity, nonunit limiting k3/k2, and vanishing phase-denominator limits are expressly outside the result and are not refuted.

nodes.title: Two-face analytic uniqueness and scale exhaustion
nodes.statement: The exact M3 hypothesis implies the admitted-class scale-exhaustiveness theorem by the corrected first and secondary Newton faces, two nonzero exact Jacobians, two analytic implicit-function steps in v = u^2, and local uniqueness for every exact branch entering the finite-interior chart.

nodes.title: Corrected M3 observable and sector-determinant closure
nodes.statement: On the exact locally unique branch of CLM-R001-FINITE-R-BRANCH-V1, which is the only branch in the admitted finite nonzero interior class of CLM-R002-FINITE-INTERIOR-SCALE-EXHAUSTIVENESS-V1, let kappa^3 = 18pi - 48/pi. There exists a finite, not numerically asserted, R0 such that for every R > R0, with u = R^(-1/6), m3D - m3N = -(4/kappa^5)u^4 + O(u^6) < 0, Chi_up = 3/2 + 4/(pi kappa) + O(u^2) > 0, det Kp_odd = (128kappa^2/pi^2)u^20 + O(u^22) = (128kappa^2/pi^2)R^(-10/3) + O(R^(-11/3)) > 0, and det Ko = (2048kappa^2/pi^4)u^26 + O(u^28) = (2048kappa^2/pi^4)R^(-13/3) + O(R^(-14/3)) > 0. All four signs hold on the exact finite-R roots through the analytic normalized-quotient and compact derivative-supremum bridge, and Chi_up is distinct from Cbr(u) = 16/(pi kappa) + O(u^2) > 0.

nodes.title: Corrected observable and determinant theorem
nodes.statement: The exact M3 hypothesis, the proved finite-R branch, the admitted-class uniqueness result, and the bound observable and sector normalizations imply the corrected observable identities, determinant coefficients, alternative R exponents, and uniform finite-R signs in CLM-SL-B4-M3-TARGET-V1.

nodes.title: Resolve the corrected B4 M3 branch contract
nodes.statement: Determine the exact finite-interior n=2 symmetric INF M3 branch, its admitted-class scale classification, m3D - m3N, the distinct upstream Chi_up relation, and both normalized sector-determinant leading terms and signs.
nodes.quantifier_contract: For the exact real n=2 symmetric INF M3 system, determine the branch and every listed M3 output for all sufficiently large finite R, with an explicit asymptotic remainder and finite-R correspondence, while allowing integer, Puiseux, logarithmic, inverse-logarithmic, mixed, and flat corrections in the admitted finite-interior class.
boundary_cases: The degenerate K0 -> 0 attractor and all other singular geometries are separated from the proved finite nonzero interior branch.
Integer-power, Puiseux, logarithmic, inverse-logarithmic, mixed, odd, flat, and non-transseries exact corrections are handled only within the stated admitted class.
The overloaded upstream scalar Chi_up is separated from the positive branch coefficient Cbr.
Kp_odd and Ko use separate exact orthonormal bases, orientations, Green normalizations, and determinant expansions.
The singular u = 0 analysis is bridged to every sufficiently large finite R by analytic remainder bounds and local branch continuation.
Spurious truncated roots, phase-denominator singularities, and local branch switching are excluded only in the proved chart.
completion_criteria: CLM-R001-FINITE-R-BRANCH-V1, CLM-R002-FINITE-INTERIOR-SCALE-EXHAUSTIVENESS-V1, and CLM-SL-B4-M3-TARGET-V1 enter the trusted closure of CTX-DEFAULT through proved inferences.

The exact branch and corrected target conclusions give K1 = C1 = 0, Chi_up > 0, det Kp_odd proportional to R^(-10/3), and det Ko proportional to R^(-13/3), thereby excluding the incompatible staged Pbuild cascade and legacy Chi_up = 0, R^(-7/2), and R^(-9/2) assertions without separate refutation nodes.

The exact proof and correction packages, normalization, reproducibility certificates, and finite-R sign bridge pass independent definition, logic, boundary, and adversarial review and are integrated by the deterministic receiver.
non_completion_conditions: Numerical roots, fits, continuation tables, or multistart failures without a proof bridge do not count.
A formal series, truncated cascade, partial lemma, or result omitting either determinant does not count.
No M3 result is reported as closing M1, M2, general G1-prime, SUP, n >= 3, global n >= 2 reflection symmetry, or a different singular chart.

nodes.title: Finite-interior Kp odd pivot and exact phase reduction
nodes.statement: At every finite-interior n=2 symmetric INF branch point with R>1 in the exact M3 contract, the normalized odd-sector matrix M=[[a0-gamma1,b0],[b0,b0-gamma2]] has b0>0 and gamma2>b0, so its lower-right entry is strictly negative and det M>0 is equivalent to S_KP=a0-gamma1+b0^2/(gamma2-b0)<0. Under the exact five-phase spectral, band, mass, and mode-index system of the proof package, S_KP<0 is equivalent to the explicit elementary inequality Phi<0 and equality is equivalent to Phi=0. Any same-sign kernel obeys the common projective-flux identity, has a unique simple downward locking point in the stated interval, and has positive endpoint impulse ratio (gamma2-b0)/b0. These are exact reductions only: the sign of Phi, det Kp_odd>0 for all finite-interior points, KO-DET, and global G1-prime remain open.

nodes.title: Exact endpoint, transfer, and Jacobi reduction proof
nodes.statement: The exact n=2 symmetric INF M3 contract and the bound odd-sector normalization imply the finite-interior pivot and phase-reduction theorem by the final-layer Green quotient calculation, the two-by-two Schur identity, exact transfer elimination with reconstruction, and the projective-flux and locking-point argument.
